anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer consistently chooses a markedly sub-optimal execution plan even though statistics are reasonable, leading to excessive I/O, CPU, or skewed access paths.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Critical engine settings (memory pools, checkpoint cadence, parallelism, etc.) are mis-tuned for the hardware and workload, so the instance’s behavior is limited more by configuration than by true resource scarcity.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Sessions serialize on hot buffer pages or latches inside the buffer manager, causing buffer-busy waits, CPU spin, and throughput collapse.

When these three root causes coincide, the database exhibits a compound failure pattern: 1) erratic plan switches or uniformly bad plans inflate logical I/O and amplify page-touch frequency; 2) mis-sized buffer pools, aggressive checkpoints, or poor parallelism settings force constant page eviction and dirty-page flush storms; 3) the flood of page accesses converges on a limited cache, driving latch spins and buffer-busy waits. Observable symptoms therefore include extreme variance in response times, sudden drops in throughput even while CPU or storage appear partially idle, surges of page-latch and log-write waits interleaved with optimizer-related recompile or plan-cache misses, and workload regressions immediately after parameter changes or engine upgrades.

Causal chain: a sub-optimal plan increases the volume and concurrency of page accesses. Because configuration parameters have left the buffer pool undersized and checkpoint cadence too aggressive, these extra pages cannot stay resident; they churn rapidly, keeping dirty-page queues full and forcing frequent flushes. The elevated churn creates hotspots (e.g., index root pages, allocation map pages) on which many sessions contend, escalating latch acquisition time. Meanwhile, mis-tuned parallelism or work-memory settings can inflate the number of concurrent workers executing the bad plan, multiplying the contention. The resulting feedback loop—bad plan → higher I/O → cache churn → latch contention → longer execution → even more concurrent executions—drives a systemic performance meltdown that is far more severe than any single anomaly acting alone.

entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
